paper.title_en: The ψ(2S) state as a subthreshold pole in electron-positron annihilation into <math altimg="si14.svg"><mrow><mi>D</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>D</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></mrow></math> final states
paper.abstract_en: By performing a fit to the merged BES 2008 and BESIII 2024 <math altimg="si15.svg"><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><msup><mi>e</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo>→</mo><mi>D</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>D</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></mrow></math> cross-section data, we find that the ψ(2S) subthreshold pole influences this process markedly. The statistical significance of the ψ(2S) as a subthreshold pole is 8σ. A fit assuming it and seven resonances excels with the fit quality characterized by <math altimg="si8.svg"><mrow><msup><mi>χ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo linebreak="goodbreak">/</mo><mtext>DOF</mtext><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>240.4</mn><mo linebreak="goodbreak">/</mo><mn>284</mn></mrow></math>, which means a p-value of 97%. The interference of resonances with the continuum provided by the subthreshold pole changes their shapes, positions, and widths.
